column1: Figure 1: This figure presents a conceptual pathway illustrating how artificial intelligence use in higher
education influences student learning through patterns of engagement and associated cognitive processes.
Artificial intelligence tools shape how students interact with learning tasks, leading to two contrasting
pathways. In the active engagement pathway, students critically interact with outputs through effortful
processing, reflection, and integration of ideas, resulting in deeper understanding, critical thinking, and the
development of competence. In the passive reliance pathway, reduced cognitive effort and externalization
of reasoning limit reflection and metacognitive monitoring, leading to superficial understanding, weaker
retention, and the potential emergence of an illusion of competence. The figure further highlights those
